summary: Sean, a visitor from Toronto, leaves his grandfather's ward feeling dejected after a recording he made there turns out to be unusable. He checks into the Lamplighter Inn in Florida, where he swims in a poorly maintained pool and meets Adele, a talkative older guest. She gives him advice about the local parks and asks about his stay, while he deflects with talk of his thesis work.
one_line: Sean, a Toronto visitor in Florida, has a ruined ward recording with his grandfather and meets the chatty Adele at a motel pool.
key_facts: Grampa's eye stopped seeking out the ward's corners and he slipped back into maintenance mode before Sean left.
Grampa came around the table for another hug and kiss before Sean left, and said 'Bye, Sean.'
Sean checked into the Lamplighter Inn, a motel on a dreary strip populated with disused water-parks and crumbling plazas.
When Sean played back his recording, he found it to be junk because the noise of the ward masked nine words in ten.
Sean tried to transcribe the recording longhand but could not keep his mind on it.
The pool water was described as piss-warm and thickly chlorinated, and felt like swimming in pungent sweat.
Sean managed one lap before crawling out to sit in a sway-backed deck-chair.
Adele, an old woman in a one-piece with a skirt and a sunhat, has skin described as the color and texture of rawhide, 'not so much tanned as baked.'
Adele said that Old Ross doesn't like dealing with the pool, so he keeps shoveling in the chlorine.
Adele told Sean, 'Don't be surprised if you're blonde in the morning.'
Adele advised Sean not to miss Universal, saying she thinks it is better than Disney.
Sean told Adele he expects to stay in Florida a couple of weeks at least and has a lot of work to do there.
Sean said he came down from Toronto, and Adele responded 'Lord, not another snowbird!'
Sean described his flight as 'a little dull, but fine.'
The text includes a stray line that a message came in from Caleb saying, 'I'm lactose intolerant,' and nothing more.
